incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PROD-INFER-LATENCY fired for inference-proxy/us-west-2 — p99 > 1.2s, count spike. Triggered at 5419090808. https://pagerduty.company/INC12345
Sam: ack. I'm on it, checking dashboards and proxy logs.
Sam: hitting the latency dashboard — big spike at 5419090750, mostly p99 and tail. No error rate increase.
Maria: @Sam any autoscaler activity? could be a hot shard or KV coldstart.
Sam: not seeing scale events. proxy pods healthy, but a few containers show long GC pauses in logs. tailing logs now:
Sam: ```
kubectl logs -n prod proxy-ffc-7f8 --since=3m | grep -i "gc pause"
2026-03-15T12:01:22Z INFO gc pause 1400ms
2026-03-15T12:02:05Z INFO gc pause 1200ms
```
Derek: hmm that's suspicious. we've had similar noisy GC causing transient p99 on that instance class before. Might be a bad JVM flag or new config.
Sophie: customer impact check: I don't see errors in frontend logs; only latency in internal canary and some batch jobs. looks low risk.
Sam: can confirm user-facing 5xx is flat. likely noisy spike affecting background inference canaries. marking impact = minimal.
incident-bot: Alert auto-resolved (recovery detected) at 5419091120.
Maria: saw it clear, but metrics look like it might bounce back. can we do a quick suppression to avoid PD churn?
Derek: I'll create a 15m pagerduty silence for this service while we triage. Command: `pd silence INC12345 --duration 15m --reason "transient GC-induced p99 spikes; triage"`
pagerduty-bot: Silence created for INC12345 by Derek (15m) — https://pagerduty.company/silences/9843
Sam: digging into recent deploys — there was a config tweak to the proxy JVM heap last hour. rolling back to previous flag on one pod for fast test.
Sam: rolling patch: ```kubectl set env deployment/proxy PROXY_JVM_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -XX:+UseG1GC" -n prod```
Sophie: monitoring traces — tail latency is improving on the patched pod within 30s.
incident-bot: New alert re-fired at 5419091450 (same symptom) — p99 spike again.
Sam: ack. looks multi-instance now, not just one pod.
Maria: we should avoid noisy paging while we confirm root cause. Derek — can you extend silence to 45m and file follow-up?
Derek: extending silence to 45m: `pd silence extend 9843 --duration 30m` — done. pagerduty-bot: Silence 9843 extended to 45m by Derek.
Sophie: confirmed no customer-facing degradation in last 30m. logs show GC churn around 12:01-12:06 and 12:12-12:14 correlating with spikes. likely a workload pattern (kv warmups).
Maria: ops note: add a short-term autoscaler policy to pre-warm KV cache for that route, and follow up with infra to tune GC flags.
Sam: filing follow-up ticket INF-3456 with initial triage, logs, and actions.
Sam: handoff to next on-call @Maria — I'll be offline for the next 2 hours. Leaving notes: check GC metrics, confirm silence, follow INF-3456.
Maria: thanks @Sam — I'll take it. monitoring dashboards and traces now. will cancel silence only if we confirm stable.
Derek: leaving a short postmortem draft in #incidents: "transient p99 flapping due to GC pattern during KV warmup; mitigated via temporary PD silence and JVM flag rollback; follow-up INF-3456"
Sophie: no customer impact observed; recommend lower PD sensitivity on internal canaries or route-specific thresholds.
Sam: thumbs up. closing this thread for now, will update INF-3456 with timeline. :thumbsup:
Maria: picking up watch. will ping if it flaps again.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC12345 remains silenced until 5419093650 (silence id 9843).
incident-bot: thread closed (auto-note) at 5419091842.
